title: Spring interruption mid-drag
prompt:
For each independent case provide diagnosis, smallest justified action, verification and limits. Do not claim execution. Treat each as a fresh product brief; cases do not authorize deployment or repository changes.

Bottom sheet uses a CSS `transition: transform 400ms linear(...)` where the `linear()` points were sampled from a spring. When the user flicks the sheet down and grabs it again mid-flight, it jumps to the end of the old curve and restarts from zero velocity. Review and repair.

checks.reason: Routing-level signal: the fix names the carried-over velocity; the rubric judges whether it seeds the new spring.
The answer must state that a linear()-sampled spring cannot retarget with velocity.
Routing-level signal only; evaluate the decision and evidence using the rubric.
Claiming linear() springs are interruptible is the anti-pattern.
Claiming linear() springs are interruptible is the anti-pattern.

rubric: A physics spring (JS or library) driven from the current position and pointer velocity replaces the sampled curve for the draggable sheet; linear() stays only for non-interruptible effects.
Verification flicks and re-grabs mid-flight and confirms continuous position and velocity, with a reduced-motion variant.
Preserve the product intent and already-authorized scope. Do not claim actual browser, mutation, installation or deploy execution from a reasoning-only answer.
Give an observable check and a meaningful limit; keyword presence alone is not acceptance.
acceptance: The response makes the justified decision for this raw case, provides a discriminating verification and states the evidence limits without inventing execution.
